_comment: Running handoff doc 01 for Claude to clean up W4 documentation, carryover classification, and wording alignment while Copilot handles SIT fix-and-close work.
title: Clean up W4 docs, reconcile carryover status, and align follow-up wording
lane: Claude Code - documentation, acceptance wording, and carryover classification
objective: Bring W4 planning and handoff docs into one coherent state while Copilot handles the SIT fix-and-close lane. Reconcile wording differences, close the remaining TASK-906 status/alignment gap, classify remaining W1-W3 carryover items clearly, and write explicit deferral notes for non-closed UI items so Codex and Copilot do not step on stale or conflicting guidance.

do_not_touch: src/frontend/index.html parity/content fix lane currently assigned to Copilot
Any direct VPS or runtime environment operation
hard_boundary.implementation_rule: This is real repo work, not a memo-only review. Update the source docs directly.

starting_context.copilot_lane_now: W4-EPIC10-SIT-FIX-AND-CLOSE-HANDOFF-01 is handling index parity/content fix plus redeploy and live proof
repo_truths_to_respect: W4 gate is already closed in principle and recorded in docs/ux/UX-FREEZE-EXPORT-CONFIGURATOR.md
main-ux-ui.html contains the current accepted W4 export/configurator implementation surface
Quick Export backend null-template path is already wired
Template Export per-run column_overrides are already wired
Configurator 3-tab shell plus real column editor exists, but some acceptance and live-proof wording still needs cleanup
known_doc_tensions: Some docs still speak as if the PO checkbox close is open, while others mark it done
Some wording still treats the Configurator as not yet built, while the repo now has a 3-tab shell and editor
TASK-906 wording alignment is still open
Clone/delete and row-grouping strategy need explicit wired-vs-deferred wording

what_to_do: 1. Reconcile W4 documentation so the current status is internally consistent across W4-EXECUTION-PLAN, W4-TASK-BOARD, UX-FREEZE-FINAL-CODEX-HANDOFF, and the Claude follow-up completion doc.
2. Close the remaining TASK-906 wording/status gap so the repo no longer mixes old W1-W3 language with the actual current completion state.
3. Classify remaining W1-W3 carryover and UX review follow-ups into clear buckets: direct W4 work, Epic 10 follow-up after W4, or backlog/customer-confirmation item.

4. Write explicit deferral wording for non-closed UI items so the repo stops implying they are either fully done or mysteriously missing. At minimum cover: template delete wiring, clone verification state, row-grouping strategy panel, and any still-open evidence-only item.

5. Keep deployment/runtime repair ownership with Copilot. If a doc mentions index.html parity or SIT runtime issues, reflect them as current Copilot-lane work rather than reassigning or re-solving them here.
6. Update W4 plan/board wording so it reflects the current reality: which items are done in repo, which are locally verified only, which need live SIT re-proof, and which are explicit follow-ups.

7. Add or refine backlog wording for customer-facing ambiguity discovered in W4 review intake, especially AP/AR split and additional template-pack questions, if those items still lack clean classification.

TASK-906 wording is aligned to current repo reality
Remaining carryover items are clearly bucketed into W4 now, later Epic 10 follow-up, or backlog/customer question
Partial items have explicit deferral notes rather than implied completion
No SIT runtime fix work is duplicated or reassigned away from Copilot
The output is committed as real doc changes in the repo, not only described in prose

final_instruction_to_claude: Finish this as direct doc work in the repo. Be decisive, keep the wording truthful, and separate active Copilot deploy/fix work from documentation and carryover cleanup.
